sources.news_title: US Army Officer Arrested in UK Over Russia Spy Claims
sources.text:
US Army Officer Arrested in UK Over Russia Spy Claims
A high-ranking US Army soldier has been arrested in England on suspicion of secretly aiding Russian intelligence, British authorities revealed Tuesday. The 41-year-old was detained near Gloucester in western England as part of a counterterrorism probe and is being held in London, NBC News reports. Police say the case centers on alleged violations of the UK's National Security Act involving access to protected information and support for a foreign intelligence service—identified as Russia.
Sources tell the AP that the man was one of dozens of American personnel serving with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, a multinational, British-led force based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucester. No sensitive information was passed to Russia, suggesting that the suspect was being watched and was arrested before any transfer could happen, sources tell the Washington Post.
FBI Director Kash Patel called the espionage-related allegations "of the utmost concern" to the US and its allies. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, a US Army counterintelligence commander, said the "alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent." British counterterrorism officials described the accusations as "very serious," but said the investigation is not tied to any other current operations, though it comes amid wider concern over hostile state activity on UK soil.

sources.news_title: US Soldier Arrested in England on Suspicion of Spying for Russia
sources.text:
A senior U.S. Army soldier suspected of spying on behalf of Russia was arrested Nov. 10 in England near a base that houses special NATO land forces, the United Kingdom’s Counter Terrorism Policing office announced.
The 41-year-old male soldier, whose identity was not released, was entrusted with sensitive information, according to a U.S. Army commanding general.
The UK’s counter-terrorism police were working with U.S. authorities, military, and the FBI.
The case showed the strength of the partnerships between the nations’ counterintelligence communities, said Commanding Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon of the U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.
“The alleged conduct of a senior [soldier], entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent,” Stinchon said. “I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office.”
The soldier was arrested in Gloucester, a city in southwest England near the Cotswolds and the Welsh border. The area is home to RAF Innsworth, managed by the British Army and serves as the headquarters for the NATO Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.
The corps is led by two British Army divisions and around 1,600 personnel from more than 20 allied nations. A request for information about the arrest sent to the corps was not immediately returned.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the allegations of espionage were “of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.”
“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message—this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners,” Patel said in a statement.
The soldier was detained under the British National Security Act 2023 and remains in custody at a London police station, according to the Metropolitan Police.
The investigation is being led by officers from the counter terrorism policing unit in London.
“This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between U.K. and U.S. authorities. The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing,” Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, of the Counter Terrorism Policing unit, said.
The case is not linked to any other ongoing investigation, according to UK officials.
The arrest is the latest in a series of national security-related arrests in England.
On Sept. 27, in connection with a security incident at Fairford airbase, British authorities arrested seven individuals suspected of working for Iran’s ruling Islamic regime.
A few weeks later in October, two Latvian men were also arrested on espionage charges after they allegedly broke into the RAF Molesworth airbase, used by the United States and NATO as an intelligence center.
McCallum described Russia as “aggressor No. 1,” accusing Russian President Vladimir Putin of lashing out at the UK and its allies, while the Kremlin’s military and intelligence services were escalating their attempts at hybrid warfare.
He attributed it to Russia’s “minimal and horrifically costly” progress in the ongoing conflict with Ukraine.
UK–Russia tensions have escalated recently as the European country vowed to send more support to Ukraine.
The U.S. brokered a two-day working-level meeting between Russia and Ukraine on Nov. 10 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, to address postwar security concerns and territorial issues.
U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner, who is leading the delegation with Steve Witkoff, said he was encouraged by the constructive discussions.
“At President [Donald Trump’s] direction, we are working to end this devastating war and establish the security arrangements necessary for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine and lasting peace across Europe,” Kushner posted on X.

sources.news_title: US Army officer held in Britain over suspected Russia-linked espionage
sources.text:
US Army officer held in Britain over suspected Russia-linked espionage
A US Army officer serving with a NATO unit in Britain has been arrested over suspected Russia-linked espionage. The case has brought British counterterrorism police, the FBI and the US military into a joint investigation.
A US Army officer serving with a NATO unit in Britain was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia, triggering a joint investigation involving British counterterrorism police, the FBI and the US military.
The 41-year-old soldier, whose identity has not been disclosed, was arrested near Gloucester in England under two provisions of the UK's National Security Act 2023. The allegations include assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information.
The suspect was serving with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester, according to US, British and NATO officials who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity. A US official identified him as an officer, while US Brigadier General Sean Stinchon, commanding general of the Army's Counterintelligence Command, described him as a senior soldier.
The Metropolitan Police said its counterterrorism officers worked closely with the FBI and the US military in the operation. FBI Director Kash Patel described the arrest as an "important arrest", saying the espionage allegations were of "utmost concern" to the United States and its allies.
The suspect remains in custody at a London police station. Police also conducted searches at two locations in Gloucestershire, around 140 kilometres west of London. Authorities have not released further details about the investigation.
The police clarified that the arrest was not connected to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations, including a suspected terror plot linked to Iran in September targeting RAF Fairford, a US-operated airbase near Gloucester.
Following that threat, the US Air Force withdrew bombers that had been used in strikes against Iran from RAF Fairford. The Air Force also relocated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall this week following another security threat, which The Wall Street Journal reported was linked to Iran.
Tuesday's arrest, however, is being investigated as a separate case involving suspected espionage connected to Russia.
The development comes amid growing concerns across Europe over Russian covert operations, including espionage, sabotage and drone incursions. Western officials have repeatedly warned about Moscow's alleged efforts to undermine security across NATO member states.
Denmark's Defence Intelligence Service recently warned that Russian President Vladimir Putin could consider military action against NATO if he believed the alliance would not respond collectively, particularly if the United States was unwilling or unable to support European allies.
Last month, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander, US General Alexus Grynkewich, said the alliance was prepared to fight back if attacked by Russia. He made the remarks during a visit to Poland, where he outlined NATO's defence preparations against a potential Russian attack.
Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, The Associated Press has tracked more than 210 incidents of sabotage and other hostile activities across Europe that Western officials have blamed on Moscow. These include alleged plots to set fire to warehouses, drone operations, attempts to kill opponents abroad, theft of defence technology and cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure.
One of the latest incidents involved an attempted drone attack on a German airport in August, which officials blamed on Russia. The incident prompted Germany to shut down a Russian consulate.

sources.news_title: U.S. soldier accused of spying linked to Russia arrested in the U.K.
sources.text:
U.S. soldier accused of spying linked to Russia arrested in the U.K.
A U.S. Army soldier has been arrested in the U.K. on suspicion that he engaged in espionage linked to Russia, British and U.S. authorities announced Tuesday.
The 41-year-old suspect was not identified, but a U.S. official told CBS News he is a senior officer based at Imjin Barracks, home to the headquarters for NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. He was arrested Tuesday near Gloucester, which is about 100 miles west of London.
The soldier is suspected of violations under Section 1 and Section 3 of the U.K.'s National Security Act of 2023 — obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service, respectively. Metropolitan Police said the suspected activity relates to Russia and they are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire — the county where the base is located — related to the investigation.
The suspect was in custody in a London police station as of Tuesday, according to Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.
"The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing," Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for the U.K.'s Counter Terrorism Policing force, said in a statement. "This activity demonstrates the strength of our UK and US law enforcement and national security partnerships, and I commend the work of all the teams involved. We will work together to take robust action against those we suspect of any criminal activity that could undermine our national security."
FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that "this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."
In an annual threat update last month, Sir Ken McCallum, the head of Britain's MI5 spy agency, accused Russia of "escalating their attempts at hybrid warfare," calling them "aggressor number one" when it comes to threats against the United Kingdom.
The arrest came as the U.S., Russia and Ukraine began a new round of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, the first such talks aimed at ending the war between Russia and Ukraine in about nine months. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the discussions "constructive and quite substantive," although it seems none of the participants expect any immediate breakthroughs, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov rejecting European demands for an immediate ceasefire.
U.K. police said the arrest was not related to "any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations," meaning it appears to be unrelated to the recent suspected plot at RAF Fairford, which officials have said is linked to Iran. The U.S. military last month removed its bombers from that base after a security incident that led to the arrests of five British men and one U.K.-Iranian national in late September. There are U.S. troops stationed at RAF Fairford, a British Royal Air Force base.
On Tuesday, the U.S. Justice Department announced that three people it accuses of being Iran-backed operatives were charged with plotting a terrorist attack at RAF Fairford. One of the suspects is in custody in New York. However, the other two are not in custody at this time, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

sources.news_title: US soldier arrested in UK over Russia-linked spying
sources.text:
A 41-year-old member of the United States Army has been arrested in the United Kingdom over alleged espionage linked to Russia.
The Metropolitan Police said the man was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing, working closely with US authorities, the US military and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
In a statement published on its website on Tuesday, the force said the suspect was arrested on suspicion of offences under Sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act 2023.
The offences relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
“The country to which the allegations relate is Russia,” the statement said.
The police said officers were also conducting searches at two locations in Gloucestershire as part of the investigation.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, described the arrest as the outcome of collaboration between British and American authorities.
“This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities,” Evans said.
“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing.
“This activity demonstrates the strength of our UK and US law enforcement and national security partnerships, and I commend the work of all the teams involved.
“We will work together to take robust action against those we suspect of any criminal activity that could undermine our national security.”
FBI reacts
The Director of the FBI, Kash Patel, also described the arrest as an important development, saying the allegations raised concerns for the security of the United States and its allies.
He disclosed this in a late night post on X on Tuesday.
“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” Patel said.
“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.
“This includes 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests from this FBI over the last 21 months – a 53 per cent increase.”
Patel thanked the UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence and the US Army Counterintelligence Command for their roles in the investigation.
Brigadier General Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of the US Army Counterintelligence Command, said the case demonstrated the importance of cooperation among security agencies.
“This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the resolve of the counterintelligence community,” he said.
“I am grateful to the UK and the FBI for their professionalism and teamwork throughout this investigation.
“The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.
“I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office.”
The Metropolitan Police said the suspect remained in custody at a London police station, while officers from Counter Terrorism Policing London were leading the investigation.
It added that the investigation was not connected to any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations.

The 41-year-old soldier, whose name has not been disclosed, was arrested near Gloucester in southwestern England as part of a counterterrorism investigation involving British and American law enforcement, authorities said.
“The country to which the allegations relate is Russia,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement.
The soldier involved was assigned to NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, a senior alliance military official said in a statement.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the case raised national security concerns.
“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” Patel said.
The arrest comes amid heightened security concerns involving American military installations in Britain, where U.S. aircraft were relocated this week following reports of a possible Iranian threat.

By Brian Melley, Konstantin Toropin and Emma Burrows
LONDON (AP) — A member of the U.S. Army was arrested Tuesday in England on suspicion of espionage related to Russia, counterterror police said. The arrest comes during heightened concern over threats to American forces stationed in Britain and tension between Moscow and much of Europe.
The 41-year-old man, who was not named, was arrested near Gloucester on suspicion of violating two sections of the National Security Act 2023: assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information.
U.S. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding general of the Army’s Counterintelligence Command, described the suspect as a senior soldier but offered no other details on his identity in a news release.
